requirements.requirement: Preserve the supplied application and status document and serve the original status endpoint only on node1 loopback TCP port 9081.
requirements.summary: The supplied files retained their baseline SHA-256 hashes. The service returned the original document from 127.0.0.1:9081, listened only on loopback, remained enabled, and recovered with unchanged data after node1 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Provide a persistent SSH tunnel exposing the node1 endpoint on node2 loopback TCP port 9082.
requirements.summary: The enabled tunnel service used SSH forwarding to 127.0.0.1:9081, listened at 127.0.0.1:9082, returned the original document, and recovered after node2 restarted with a different boot identity.

requirements.requirement: Prevent other cluster hosts from gaining direct access to either application listener.
requirements.summary: Both listeners were directly observed on loopback only. Cross-node requests to node1:9081 and node2:9082 through their cluster addresses were denied after the final restarts.

requirements.requirement: Recover the tunnel after a brief SSH connection interruption without manual recreation.
requirements.summary: The healthy tunnel baseline was captured, its server-side SSH session was terminated, and node2 automatically produced new process IDs, incremented the service restart count, restored port 9082, and returned the expected document hash.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the supplied status document and application under /srv/legacy2/ssh-local-service-tunnel.
requirements.summary: Baseline and final checks on both managed nodes show unchanged hashes for serve.py and status/index.html at the supplied path.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with that platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64. The solution used the installed Python 3, OpenSSH, systemd, and runuser facilities; final package-health observations were clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by fixed lifecycle observations, and recovered services, data, listeners, and cross-node functionality. Operational hygiene is good overall, with a deduction for two transient unsuccessful security-policy experiments and one unnecessary hardening removal retained in the final tunnel service.
limitations: No explicit package transaction history was captured; platform snapshots, unchanged OS/kernel observations, and successful DNF consistency checks provide strong but not exhaustive support that the installed platform was preserved.
Requirement application_node1 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1
Requirement preserve_supplied_tree cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1, seeded-state-node2

operational_hygiene.summary: Final state was clean: no failed services, package health remained sound, temporary diagnostic output was cleaned, SELinux remained enforcing, and only the required loopback listeners were added. Three unnecessary troubleshooting mutations were identified: cmd-1eee28c9fd2940ac removed NoNewPrivileges from the tunnel unit while testing a hypothesis; that change did not fix execution and remained in the final unit, unnecessarily reducing hardening. cmd-83490e4fbe304dcd created a collected transient unit to test an explicit SELinux context; it failed and left no observed residue. cmd-06b477b10b1246c9 temporarily disabled SELinux dontaudit rules and restarted the tunnel while seeking AVC evidence; policy suppression was restored with semodule -B and no final residue is shown. The latter two were bounded and reverted/transient, while the retained hardening removal warrants the main deduction.
